title: Scratch-run compact dashboard (personal)
content:
Purpose: tiny, fast reference sheet for morning iteration runs. Keep it short, snapshot results, and jot followups. Not exhaustive.

Columns (CSV): experiment_id,date,model,quant,hw,batch,avg_input_tokens,avg_output_tokens,total_tokens,p50_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,kv_cache_enabled,notes,next_steps

Rows:
exp-2026-02-28-a,2026-02-28,lama-7b,q4_0,A10G,1,32,48,80,42,88,0.023,true,"stable-ish p50, p95 spiky on long contexts; cache reduced repeated-prefix runs by ~35%","re-run with cache TTL=20s; add longer prefix test"
exp-2026-03-01-b,2026-03-01,owl-13b,q8_0,H100,4,64,128,192,110,240,0.045,false,"good throughput at batch=4 but p95 high for tails; shaves cost at high batch","try continuous-batching knob + microbatched kv store"
exp-2026-03-05-c,2026-03-05,redwood-mini-1.3b,f16,A10G,8,16,32,48,28,64,0.011,true,"cheap, excellent latency; acceptable quality for smoke tests","add to quickstart templates"
exp-2026-03-08-d,2026-03-08,open-llama-3-70b,q4_0,H100,1,128,256,384,210,470,0.12,true,"very expensive; fallback candidate only. p95 unstable when kv not warmed","validate warmup policy + fallback route to smaller model"

Quick notes / observations:
- KV cache matters: for repeated-prefix flows (search snippets, multi-message chat warmups) we see 20-40% token savings; affects both latency and cost.
- Batching tradeoffs: batch=4 on H100 gave 2.7x throughput vs batch=1 but p95 increased ~2x. For user-facing low-concurrency it's a net win to keep batch=1. For backend async generation, batch=4/8 is preferred.
- Cost calc: naive cost_per_1k_tokens_usd from infra pricing + quantization multiplier. Useful to flag when > $0.05/1k (alert threshold).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a tiny script to convert these rows -> CSV and push to the team perf dashboard (PR exists but not wired: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/1289).
- Should we include GPU memory pressure field? Observed OOM with llama-7b + batch=8 on A10G in last run. Add "gpu_mem_gb" column next iteration.
- Confirm cluster autoscaler impact on cold-start p95 (Ravi to check with SRE; ticket JIRA-ENG-2124).

Scratch calculations (very rough):
- Example: exp-2026-02-28-a total tokens 80 at cost 0.023/1k -> cost per request = 80/1000 * 0.023 = $0.00184. If 10k requests/day -> $18.4/day.
- If KV reduces tokens 35% -> effective tokens = 52 -> cost ~ $0.0012/request -> daily $12.4 (saving ~$6/day for this microflow).

Session log (short):
- 2026-03-09 morning: ran sweep with TTL [5s,20s,60s]. 20s seemed best tradeoff. Noted p95 drop only when worker warmups were present.
- 2026-03-10 afternoon: sanity check on redwood-mini -> will propose add to quickstart; written note for docs.

Next steps (short checklist):
- [ ] Add gpu_mem_gb column next run
- [ ] Wire CSV->perf dashboard (follow up on PR 1289)
- [ ] Create tiny eval prompt set to check quality when using q4_0 vs f16 (sample 120 prompts)
- [ ] Sync with SRE on autoscaler cold-start regressions (assign to Ravi)

Notes-to-self: keep entries terse. Use this as single-source quick reference before demos. Archive monthly into /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/perf-archive if run count > 30.

End of sheet.
